Sources, alignment and limitations

CNN official methodology: seven equally weighted market indicators, including S&P 500 relative to its 125-day average and stocks versus bonds over 20 sessions. Official CNN historical endpoint. ETF returns: Bloomberg Desktop API, gross dividend-reinvested total-return indices.

Pearson and Spearman; primary predictive entry is next-session close, then +1/+5/+20/+60 ETF sessions. Same-day correlation is not predictive. Circular moving-block bootstrap, 500 repetitions, block=max(20,horizon). Separate years and 2021–2024 / 2025–2026 windows; no threshold optimization. One CNN date is missing (2026-03-12); it remains missing. The duplicated latest-day observation was resolved by timestamp. Historical UTC-midnight stamps are treated as date labels, not shifted to the preceding US date.

  • CNN is partly constructed from stock momentum, breadth, volatility and stocks-versus-bonds; same-day association is endogenous.
  • Retrospectively downloaded, potentially revised history; immutable publication-time CNN vintages are unavailable.
  • Current day excluded from the historical study even after regular close; latest CNN displayed separately.
  • Price-level correlation can be misleading because prices trend while the index is bounded. It is diagnostic only.
  • Overlapping forward returns reduce independent observations; block intervals and non-overlapping checks are provided.
  • Multiple horizons and regimes are exploratory; confidence intervals are not adjusted for multiple testing.
  • QQQ/SPY means the ratio of gross total-return indices (relative performance), not the P&L of a dollar-neutral long/short portfolio.
  • No transaction costs, trading strategy or causal claim. Sample starts February 2021 and excludes the 2020 crash.

Missing values are never filled with zero; current-day CNN is shown only as context. Local raw snapshots, date-level calculations and input hashes are retained for audit.

How to look for the next case
  1. Detect topic diffusion: ticker + product + catalyst aliases; 6h / 24h / 72h windows; feed-normalised mentions; unique and newly participating authors; company/partner/news concentration.
  2. Read the change in conviction: compare each source with its own earlier view. Keep firsthand usage, monetization evidence, investment opinion, client inquiries and actual reported flows separate. Deduplicate the event across brokers.
  3. Map participation and position size: breadth of HF ownership, position sizing, LO sponsorship and PB net exposure are distinct. Missing holdings stay unknown; enthusiasm alone does not create a crowded-position label.
  4. Test a frozen signal before the open: log the cutoff and available source snapshot; compare next-open returns at +1/+3/+5/+20 sessions and later attention/desk diffusion. Control for prior return, broad/sector move, earnings and research changes. Include failed alerts and matched no-alert stocks.

This overlay implements topic mappings, source-separated counts, a reviewed META desk/tone timeline and descriptive price parallels. Intraday collection, generic semantic desk labelling, event-wide deduplication and prospective alerts still require implementation and evaluation. There is no new fitted composite or automatic trade recommendation.

Coverage, timestamps and competing catalysts
  • User-collected account sample, not the whole of X. Other accounts are not certified independent; affiliation list is incomplete. No follower/like weights or engagement captured after the move.
  • fetched_at is overwritten when engagement is refreshed, not immutable first_seen. A fetch before cutoff proves availability by then; a later fetch does not prove absence before cutoff. No full historical point-in-time backtest.
  • 6,733 message metadata records scanned since Sep 7 in the primary Outlook store; 314 candidate bodies selected by specialist sender/subject. Online archive and attachments not exhaustively read; 11 META notes context-reviewed.
  • Case-selected retrospective description, not a validated leading factor. QQQ is a broad growth benchmark, not a sector-neutral hedge.
  • Bloomberg Desktop API / PX_LAST and PX_OPEN; downloaded 21 Sep 2026 after US regular close; same-day vendor marks, not audited final close

Meta launched Muse on September 8, before the observed weekend. Wells Fargo raised its target to $796 from $640 before Monday's open. Connect on September 23 was another expectation catalyst. The weekend is a diffusion case, not a causal attribution of Monday's return.

All 55 weekend posts have a stored fetch timestamp before the Monday 08:30 ET cut. This supports pre-open availability in the existing collection, not a claim that this overlay issued an alert at that time. The original weekly tracker remains dated separately below.

What this measures: discussion intensity and agreement. Actual crowded holdings require fund positions, flows or lending data. The chronological test did not validate this candidate as a positive predictor of further attention growth; four-week return evidence is weak. A high score is a research flag, not a buy or sell signal.

Calculation, data dates and improvements
  • Pressure candidate: 35% acceleration percentile + 30% abnormal-attention percentile + 20% sentiment-change percentile + 15% positive-share percentile. Percentiles use up to 252 strictly prior sessions, with at least 60 valid observations. No weights are fitted to returns; no missing component is silently reweighted.
  • Attention: publication count divided by total counts in the available company universe. Compare current 5-session mean share with the prior 20 sessions, excluding the current five. Acceleration compares current and previous five. A 0.1 basis-point regulariser avoids division by tiny values; sparse inputs are flagged.
  • Coverage: at least 4/5 and 16/20 observations for average features; exact five-day mention totals require all five. At least 25 publications and five classified positive/negative publications per five sessions for the candidate. Counts are vendor coverage, not all of X.
  • Original posts: exact-text deduplication, no retweets; wire posts remain in attention and are removed from opinion. Mention share uses all original posts in the collected feed as denominator. Unique handles, effective author count, top-author share and near-copy clusters remain separate.
  • Stance extraction: conservative company-specific clauses, multi-company and recognised sarcasm abstention, operating news separated from investment stance and self-reported portfolio action. Equal-weight author/source votes and sparse-data shrinkage. Rule based; no independent semantic-classifier validation yet.
  • Source baseline: current stance minus the same author's prior stance, only with five prior classified posts. Missing calibration stays N/A. The source history is short.
  • Earnings vintages: only explicit calendar-year period labels are stored for future comparisons. Rolling 1BF EPS is excluded from the new score. There is only one current vintage; no fabricated historical revision series.
  • Validation: 2024–2025 and 2026 reported separately; earlier-period outcomes crossing the split are purged. Friday signals use next session's close for entry, then 5 or 20 sessions. Weekly rank IC, momentum/current-attention controls, block confidence intervals and non-overlapping subsamples are reported. No sector controls without reliable classifications; no cost-adjusted tradable return claim.
Remaining limitations and next evidence
  • There is no direct historical label for long positioning or portfolio overlap. Short interest is shown only as delayed context in the exported data, with a conservative 20-calendar-day publication lag; actual release timestamps are unavailable.
  • The cached universe is today's universe. Delistings and historical members are absent. Vendor histories may be revised, and corporate-action/total-return treatment is not independently verified.
  • Near-copy clustering cannot reliably identify a shared underlying event when sources paraphrase it. The review queue is seeded for analyst labelling; it is not represented as independently human-labelled.
  • Collected X author history is only the available recent snapshot, and ingestion timestamps are unavailable. We cannot backtest historical access to each post or validate author-diffusion leading power yet.
  • No unattended schedule was changed. The local rebuild reads a fresh snapshot when supplied; alerts on freshness and coverage are saved on every run. Immutable output snapshots support future prospective checks.
  • The next meaningful proof is prospective: freeze this version, accumulate daily source snapshots and actual positioning labels, then test incremental forecasts versus attention and price baselines without retuning on the test period.

Research context: NBER · Attention, Social Interaction, and Investor Attraction to Lottery Stocks. Evidence from social attention motivates testing; it does not validate this tracker or its current universe.
